references.text: The veil (הַפָּרֹכֶת) that separated the holy place from the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle, mentioned here as a boundary that a priest with a defect could not cross.
The altar (הַמִּזְבֵּחַ) which priests had to approach in purity; here priests with defects are forbidden from approaching it.
The context describing which defects disqualify a priest from offering food for his God.
A priest with a defect may eat of the holy bread, but may not perform priestly service at the altar.
Warning against profaning (יְחַלֵּל) the holy offerings; the same verb is used regarding profaning the sanctuary.
The Lord sanctifies (מְקַדֵּשׁ) the tabernacle and the priests, a concept parallel to the conclusion of the verse.
The Lord declares Himself as the one who sanctifies Israel (אֲנִי יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם), parallel to מְקַדְּשָׁם.
In Ezekiel's temple vision, no foreigner with an uncircumcised heart is to enter the sanctuary.
The inner room behind the veil could only be entered by the high priest, and only once a year.
Through Christ, believers now have bold access to the Most Holy Place through the veil.
